findings.message:
[P1] Invalidate the pending defaults debounce on target changes

If an edit schedules the 500 ms save and the operator changes `baseSelect` before it fires, `clearDefaultsSaveQueue()` only resets the flag; the pending callback still enters this new branch and queues a save for the new target. The subsequent load can then POST freshly loaded or fallback values to the newly selected gateway; cancel or invalidate the pending debounce when the target changes.

static/admin.js:10481-10483

[P2] Reconcile filtered key views after concurrent edits

When an expiry PATCH response arrives after another input changed during the request, `inputsUnchanged` is false and this rerender is skipped. `updateKeyStatus()` only changes the existing row's state and text, so the key remains in the old Active/Expired tab and an extended key gets no new expiry timer until another reload or queued save.

static/admin.js:7363-7363

[P3] Give live expired rows a warning accent

The new status refresh writes `data-state="expired"`, but `static/style.css` still defines accents only for `active`, `warning`, and `revoked`; rows that expire while open or are edited to an expired date therefore fall back to the muted accent instead of the warning accent. Use the warning state or add an expired-row rule.

static/admin.js:7145-7148

reviews.summary: The patch retains a cross-target defaults-save race and incomplete live key rendering.

evidence: The pending debounced defaults save is not invalidated by the target-change handler, so the candidate can still queue a POST for the newly selected gateway.
The candidate leaves static/style.css without an expired-row accent rule while static/admin.js assigns data-state="expired".

The added JavaScript tests only regex-match source text and do not exercise delayed/reload saves, revoke cancellation, expired unrevoke behavior, or expired-key rendering; the route list also omits the revoke and unrevoke endpoints.

findings.message:
[P1] Anchor V3 request TTLs to the usage window

The request-row type has no `window_reset_at_ms`, so this always falls back to `reserved_at_ms`. The source writer expires both the request and its aggregate from `window_reset_at_ms` (`src/api-key-policy.ts:747-750`); a request near the start of a long/current window can therefore be skipped while its window is imported, dropping lifecycle history and potentially leaving `reserved_requests` inconsistent. Reconstruct the matching window reset or skip the related state instead of using the reservation timestamp.

src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:282-286

reviews.summary: The migration adds bounded TTLs and Kernel V2 reconciliation, but V3 request retention uses the wrong timestamp.

evidence: `src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:265-302` adds bounded TTL/skip handling, and `:324-353` imports and reconciles active Kernel V2 reservations.

`src/cache/kv-migration-usage.ts:659-724` and `src/kernel/quota-reservations.ts:114-154` validate reservation identity, scope, state, lease/window ordering, reset consistency, orphan rows, and aggregate mismatches.

`src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:282-286` uses `reserved_at_ms` for V3 request expiry even though the source writes expiry from the matching usage window reset, so the candidate can omit valid quota lifecycle rows while retaining their aggregate.

findings.message:
[P1] Preserve reverse lookup for already-flattened tool choices

When the compatibility form supplies a synthesized name such as `{ type: "function", function: { name: "ns_lookup" } }`, `toolNames` contains `ns_lookup` mapped to `{ name: "lookup", namespace: "ns" }`, but this loop compares against `original.name` and falls through to returning `ns_lookup`. This breaks the existing reverse-mapping contract and the unchanged `deepseek-catalog-branch-coverage.test.ts` assertion; retain the map-key lookup while adding the namespace-aware path.

src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:652-655

reviews.summary: The namespace-aware choice works for original name plus namespace, but regresses existing flattened-name compatibility choices.

evidence: src/deepseek/chat-projection.ts:647-669 adds a namespace-aware lookup that translates the colliding original identity `{name: "now", namespace: "clock"}` to `clock_now`.
tests/deepseek-responses.test.ts:212-245 covers the top-level/namespace collision and asserts both the synthesized choice and the returned function call retain `name: "now"` and `namespace: "clock"`.

findings.message:
[P1] Keep paid-fallback pending markers durable

When an unresolved `paid_fallback/v3/pending` marker is migrated, this branch applies the request-log retention TTL. The admission writer stores these markers without `expireIn`, and `getPaidFallbackOutstandingV3` treats any marker as outstanding, so an unresolved migrated request can lose its marker after a year and become deletable without reconciliation. Do not expire pending markers here.

src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:303-304

[P2] Preserve TTLs for all expiring migration groups

For importable `paid_fallback/ledger` and `embeddings/idempotency/v1` rows, `migrationExpireIn` reaches this fallback and returns `null`, so the subsequent write has no `expireIn`. Their source writers use finite retention periods, meaning migration turns stale ledger and idempotency data permanent instead of reconstructing or skipping it; add explicit cases or skip rows whose expiry cannot be safely reconstructed.

src/cache/kv-migration-base.ts:315-315

reviews.summary: The importer applies one-year TTLs to durable pending markers and leaves other expiring migration groups permanent.

evidence: The candidate adds TTL reconstruction for API-key V3, paid-fallback V3 request/window/lease, and Kernel V2 rows, but importable paid-fallback ledger and embeddings idempotency rows still fall through to the no-TTL path, while paid-fallback pending markers receive an incorrect TTL.
The candidate adds Kernel V2 reservation reconciliation and validation for identity/reset and aggregate consistency, with migration tests for V3 expiry and reservation aggregation.
The base already retains V2 quota exports and history readers in src/kernel/usage.ts, so the legacy-export portion appears satisfied at the base, but the retention acceptance remains unmet.

findings.message:
[P1] Preserve the Edit button when rebuilding key actions

`editBtn` is appended to `actionRow`, then `renderKeyActions` immediately clears the row with `textContent = ""` and only adds revoke/restore/delete controls. Every API-key row therefore loses its Edit button, preventing expiry and other key edits.

static/admin.js:6833-6833

[P1] Make the API-key test match and exercise behavior

This assertion requires `if (statusKind !== "revoked")`, but the implementation uses `if (nextStatusKind !== "revoked")`, so the new test fails every run. Even after correcting that name, the surrounding checks only match source text rather than rendering a row or exercising delayed saves, confirmation cancellation, or the unrevoke warning.

tests/static-assets.test.ts:811-811

[P2] Cover revoke and unrevoke in the cache matrix

The route matrix jumps from `/admin/api-keys/changes` to kernel routes and omits the defined `POST /admin/api-keys/revoke` and `POST /admin/api-keys/unrevoke` endpoints, so a cache-header regression on either mutation route would pass the purported route-wide test.

tests/static-assets.test.ts:768-773

reviews.summary: The patch introduces an API-key editing regression and a failing, incomplete test suite.

evidence: `renderKeyActions` clears the action row after the Edit button is appended, so API-key rows cannot be edited and the expiry-edit requirement is not fulfilled.
The new API-key test expects `statusKind` while the implementation uses `nextStatusKind`, making the test fail; its source-text assertions also do not implement the requested behavioral tests.
The route-wide cache test omits the revoke and unrevoke admin endpoints.

findings.message:
[P1] Declare the imported text asset for TypeScript

The only asset declaration in `types/assets.d.ts` covers `*.md`, while this import targets a `.txt` file and `tsconfig.json` includes test files. The strict TypeScript gate will therefore report this module as unresolved before the evidence test can run; add a `*.txt` declaration or use a supported file-reading path.

tests/sentinel-review-evidence.test.ts:4-6

[P1] Register the cases with Bun's test API

The repository executes test files with Bun and supplies Bun/Node typings, but both cases are registered with `Deno.test` at lines 17 and 50. `Deno` is not declared in this checkout, so strict checking fails; import `test` from `bun:test` and use it for both tests.

tests/sentinel-review-evidence.test.ts:17-17

reviews.summary: The SHA records are populated, but the added evidence test cannot pass the repository's strict Bun/TypeScript gates.

evidence: The evidence archive records full reviewed head and base SHAs plus reviewer values in its review identity table at lines 29-42.
The canonical backlog adds a full Reviewed base SHA column for every row at lines 8-38.
The required negative check is not executable in this Bun/strict-TypeScript checkout because the test imports an undeclared .txt asset and uses Deno.test.
